### Reuel's block Question 4: "how have post-graduation earnings changed over the same period?"

#### Columns important to my question

## 1.Identifiers & Matching

1.  "*UNITID*", \# Unique institution identifier

2.  "*INSTNM*", \# Institution name

## 2. Institutional Type & Filtering

"*CONTROL*":

1 = Public,

2 = Private Nonprofit,

3 = Private For-Profit "PREDDEG",

Predominant degree (3 = Predominantly Bachelor's)

## 3. Post-Graduation Earnings (Primary Response Variables)

1.  "*MD_EARN_WNE_P6*", \# Median earnings working & not enrolled, 6 yrs post-entry

2.  "*MD_EARN_WNE_P10*", \# Median earnings working & not enrolled, 10 yrs post-entry

3.  "*GT_25K_P10*", \# Fraction earning \> \$25k (in 2014 constant dollars)

## 4. Context for Financial Investment

1.  "*DEBT_MDN*", \# Median cumulative student debt at graduation

2.  "*NPT4_PUB*", \# Average net price for public institutions

3.  "*NPT4_PRIV*" \# Average net price for private institutions

```{r}
project.dir <- "C:/Projects" 
dataset.dir <- file.path(project.dir, "Datasets",
                         "College_Scorecard_Raw_Data_06102026", 
                         "College_Scorecard_Raw_Data_06032026") 
outputs.dir <- file.path(project.dir, "Output")
setwd(project.dir)
list.files(dataset.dir, pattern = "MERGED")

year9_10 <- read_csv(
  file.path(dataset.dir, "MERGED2009_10_PP.csv"),
   col_select = c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "PREDDEG", "MD_EARN_WNE_P10","MD_EARN_WNE_P6","GT_25K_P10","DEBT_MDN","NPT4_PUB","NPT4_PRIV"),
  na = c("","NA","PrivacySuppressed")
)

year14_15 <- read_csv(
  file.path(dataset.dir, "MERGED2014_15_PP.csv"),
  col_select = c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "PREDDEG", "MD_EARN_WNE_P10","MD_EARN_WNE_P6","GT_25K_P10","DEBT_MDN","NPT4_PUB","NPT4_PRIV"),
  na = c("","NA","PrivacySuppressed")
)
year20_21 <- read_csv(
  file.path(dataset.dir, "MERGED2020_21_PP.csv"),
 col_select = c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "PREDDEG", "MD_EARN_WNE_P10","MD_EARN_WNE_P6","GT_25K_P10","DEBT_MDN","NPT4_PUB","NPT4_PRIV"),
```

```{r}
#checking data types

class(all_years$GT_25K_P10)

class(all_years$MD_EARN_WNE_P6)

class(all_years$DEBT_MDN)

class(all_years$NPT4_PUB)

class(all_years$NPT4_PRIV)

#Fixing NA values

  mutate(NPT4_combined = coalesce(NPT4_PUB, NPT4_PRIV))
```

## Accounting for equal spending power then graphing

```{r}
#I forgot to include inflation with these graphs 
ggplot(all_years, aes(x = CONTROL, y = MD_EARN_WNE_P6)) + geom_boxplot()
ggplot(all_years, aes(x = CONTROL, y = MD_EARN_WNE_P10)) + geom_boxplot()
ggplot(all_years, aes(x = CONTROL, y = GT_25K_P10)) + geom_boxplot()

#formula to adjust for inflation ADD NPT4 for pub & priv into formula 
# inflation based on 2020/2021 
#found from the bureau of labor statistics | CPI - consumer price index
#formula - multiplier = CPI target year(2020)/ CPI Cohort year
#i found out that the GT_25k variable is the only adjusted variable so that's why i created this formula | GT_25k isn't a recorded variable past 2012 
all_years <- all_years %>%
  mutate( #check for already adjusted inflation
    inflation_adjust = case_when(
      year == "2009-2010" ~ 1.206,
      year == "2014-2015" ~ 1.093,
      year == "2020-2021" ~ 1.000
    ),
    NPT4_combined = coalesce(NPT4_PUB,NPT4_PRIV),
    MD_EARN_WNE_P6_real  = MD_EARN_WNE_P6 * inflation_adjust,
    MD_EARN_WNE_P10_real = MD_EARN_WNE_P10 * inflation_adjust,
    DEBT_MDN_real        = DEBT_MDN * inflation_adjust,
    NPT4_real = NPT4_combined * inflation_adjust,
    #formula to get a gauge of efficiency 
    earn_to_debt_ratio = MD_EARN_WNE_P10_real / DEBT_MDN_real
  )

# Create 4-year Bachelor subset for valid comparison
bachelor_schools <- all_years %>%
  filter(PREDDEG == "Bachelor's" & !is.na(MD_EARN_WNE_P10_real))

# 1. Ten-Year Real Earnings Trajectory
ggplot(bachelor_schools, aes(x = CONTROL, y = MD_EARN_WNE_P10_real, fill = year)) + 
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.2) + 
  labs( 
    title = "6 year post-entry median earnings by institution type",
    x = "Institution type",
    y = "Median earnings(inflation accounted to 2020 standards)"
  )

# 2. Six-Year Real Earnings Trajectory
ggplot(bachelor_schools, aes(x = CONTROL, y = MD_EARN_WNE_P6_real, fill = year)) + 
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.2) + 
  labs( 
    title = "10 year post-entry median earnings by institution type",
    x = "Institution type",
    y = "Median earnings(inflation accounted to 2020 standards)"
  )

# 3. Median Real Debt by Sector
ggplot(bachelor_schools, aes(x = CONTROL, y = DEBT_MDN_real, fill = year)) + 
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.2) + 
  labs( 
    title = "median debt by institution type",
    x = "Institution type",
    y = "Median debt"
  )
#won't use this graph
ggplot(bachelor_schools, aes(x = CONTROL, y = GT_25K_P10, fill = year)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Share of Students Earning >$25k (10 Years Post-Entry)",
    x = "Institutional Control",
    y = "Percentage Earning >$25k",
  )

```

## Answers/notes :

1\. Why I had to make the inflation formula: When looking at the data dictionary, GT_25K_P10 was already adjusted to 2014 constant dollars by the Department of Education, but none of the actual dollar variables (MD_EARN_WNE_P6, MD_EARN_WNE_P10, DEBT_MDN, NPT4) were adjusted for inflation across the three cohort files. Because 2009, 2014, and 2020 dollars don't have the same purchasing power, I used the BLS CPI-U numbers to adjust all the dollar amounts to constant 2020 dollars so we could compare them fairly.

2.Why there were so many NAs in NPT4_PUB and NPT4_PRIV: A school can only be public or private—it can't be both. So if a school is private, the public net price column is automatically empty (NA), and if it's public, the private column is empty (NA). Instead of dropping those rows and losing data, I used coalesce() to combine them into one NPT4_combined variable.

3.Overall wage trend (real purchasing power): After adjusting for inflation to 2020 dollars, median earnings didn't steadily go up.

4.The 2014–15 drop: Across all sectors, earnings took a noticeable hit for the 2014–15 cohort (dropping by roughly $7,000$ for public 4-year schools in the 10-year metric, p \< 0.001\$).

5.10-Year earnings stayed flat over the decade: By 2020–21, 10-year real median earnings for public colleges only increased by about $313$ compared to 2009–10. Because the $p$-value was 0.72, that difference is not statistically significant—meaning real 10-year wages basically stagnated.

6.6-Year earnings saw a small real gain: For 6-year median earnings at public colleges, there was a statistically significant increase of about +$1,893$ by 2020–21 (p = 0.0095).

7.Public and private nonprofits held up, but for-profits dropped hard: Public and private nonprofit grads generally kept their purchasing power over the decade, but private for-profit bachelor's programs took a massive loss, dropping by over $11,600$ in real earnings relative to public schools (p \< 0.001).


### Brian's block Question 5: "Do completion rates track with cost? Are students paying more but finishing less?"

```{r}
# my own setup so my block runs no matter what's above it
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
options(scipen = 999)

q5_data_dir <- file.path("Datasets",
                         "College_Scorecard_Raw_Data_06102026",
                         "College_Scorecard_Raw_Data_06032026")

```

#### Columns important to my question

1. *UNITID*, *INSTNM*: identifiers
2. *CONTROL*, *PREDDEG*: institution type and predominant degree
3. *C150_4*: completion rate within 6 years at 4-year schools (main response variable)
4. *NPT4_PUB*, *NPT4_PRIV*: average net price (combined into one variable)
5. *COSTT4_A*: average cost of attendance
6. *PCTPELL*: share of students on Pell grants (control for student income level)

```{r}
q5_cols <- c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "PREDDEG", "C150_4",
             "NPT4_PUB", "NPT4_PRIV", "COSTT4_A", "PCTPELL")

# read as character first so the three years stack without type errors
q5_read_year <- function(file, label) {
  read_csv(file.path(q5_data_dir, file),
           col_select = all_of(q5_cols),
           na = c("", "NA", "NULL", "PrivacySuppressed"),
           col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
    mutate(year = label)
}

q5_all <- bind_rows(
  q5_read_year("MERGED2009_10_PP.csv", "2009-2010"),
  q5_read_year("MERGED2014_15_PP.csv", "2014-2015"),
  q5_read_year("MERGED2020_21_PP.csv", "2020-2021")
) %>%
  mutate(
    across(-c(INSTNM, year), as.numeric),
    # same CPI multipliers (2020 dollars)
    inflation_adjust = case_when(
      year == "2009-2010" ~ 1.206,
      year == "2014-2015" ~ 1.093,
      year == "2020-2021" ~ 1.000
    ),
    NPT4_real = coalesce(NPT4_PUB, NPT4_PRIV) * inflation_adjust,
    NPT4_k    = NPT4_real / 1000,  # in $1,000s for readable regression output
    COST_real = COSTT4_A * inflation_adjust,
    CONTROL = factor(CONTROL, levels = 1:3,
                     labels = c("Public", "Private Nonprofit", "Private For-Profit"))
  )

# bachelor's schools with completion + net price in ALL 3 years (same type each year)
q5_bach <- q5_all %>%
  filter(PREDDEG == 3, !is.na(C150_4), !is.na(NPT4_real)) %>%
  group_by(UNITID) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(year) == 3, n_distinct(CONTROL) == 1) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Comparing net price and completion by year and institution type

```{r}
q5_summary <- q5_bach %>%
  group_by(year, CONTROL) %>%
  summarize(n_schools      = n(),
            med_net_price  = median(NPT4_real),
            med_completion = median(C150_4),
            .groups = "drop")
q5_summary
```

```{r}
# arrow moving right and down = paying more, finishing less
ggplot(q5_summary, aes(med_net_price, med_completion, color = CONTROL)) +
  geom_path(aes(group = CONTROL), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"))) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = substr(year, 1, 4)), vjust = -1, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "Median net price vs. completion rate, 2009-10 to 2020-21",
       x = "Median net price (2020 dollars)", y = "Median 6-year completion rate",
       color = "Institution type")
```

## Regression model

```{r}
# completion over time, controlling for net price and Pell share
q5_model <- lm(C150_4 ~ NPT4_k + PCTPELL + year * CONTROL, data = q5_bach)
summary(q5_model)
```

## Same schools in 2009-10 vs. 2020-21

```{r}
q5_matched <- q5_bach %>%
  filter(year %in% c("2009-2010", "2020-2021")) %>%
  select(UNITID, CONTROL, year, NPT4_real, C150_4) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = c(NPT4_real, C150_4)) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(price_change = `NPT4_real_2020-2021` - `NPT4_real_2009-2010`,
         comp_change  = `C150_4_2020-2021` - `C150_4_2009-2010`,
         outcome = case_when(
           price_change > 0  & comp_change < 0 ~ "Paying more, finishing less",
           price_change > 0                    ~ "Paying more, finishing more",
           comp_change < 0                     ~ "Paying less, finishing less",
           TRUE                                ~ "Paying less, finishing more"))

q5_matched %>%
  count(CONTROL, outcome) %>%
  group_by(CONTROL) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
```

## Answers/notes:

1\. Data choices: C150_4 = % finishing a bachelor's within 6 years. Net price is combined (public/private) and adjusted to 2020 dollars. Note: completion is lagged ~6 years behind price.

2\. Price stayed flat: Real net price barely changed for public (~$14,300) and private nonprofit (~$22,500). For-profits got cheaper ($30,400 → $23,200).

3\. Completion went up: Public 45% → 52%, private nonprofit 55% → 58%. For-profits were lowest 37% → 33%.

4\. Regression: Public completion rose ~10 points by 2020-21 (p < 0.001), even after controlling for price and Pell share. Price barely matters (+0.5 points per $1,000); Pell share matters a lot (more low-income students = lower completion).

5\. Same schools over time: Only ~8% of public schools and ~19% of private nonprofits were paying more but finishing less. Only for-profit schools (28) were in this data so it is hard to trust.

6\. Answer: No, students aren't paying more and finishing less. Price held steady while completion improved. For-profits are the weak spot but this is also the only type of school that went down in price.
